Hi Jonas / Redwood team,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we start to scope AtlasMed's private VPC deployment we need a more prescriptive custody assurance plan focused on two items for our security board:

1) Ephemeral KEK fallback: if customer BYOK fails (operator error, HSM offline), what is the documented fallback path, how that path is gated, and what controls prevent accidental use of fallback keys. We need sequence diagrams and explicit operator handoffs.

2) Telemetry gating & audit evidence: which telemetry events are emitted during key rotation/unwrap, what immutability guarantees exist for audit logs, and how you present tamper-evidence for our auditors (hash chains, SIEM hooks, retention controls).

Can you share a short mutual action plan and any artifacts (sequence diagram, matrix of controls, runbook snippets) we can circulate to our compliance team? Targeting an internal review by 2026-09-15.

Hi Anika — thanks for the clear ask. Summary and attachments below; I attached a short matrix and a sequence diagram to start.

Quick summary (top-level):
- Fallback model: Redwood supports a strictly-audited operator fallback that uses a short-lived escrow KEK only when the customer-initiated unseal (BYOK HSM) is unavailable AND two independent attestation gates pass (operator + customer delegate). The escrow KEK is stored in an HSM with split custody and is rotated weekly when in escrow state.
- Gating: two-person operator approval (with MFA push) + customer delegate explicit approval via a signed webhook from a pre-provisioned callback endpoint. No plaintext key export is possible; unseal occurs inside HSM boundary.
- Telemetry & audit: every unseal, rotation, and fallback event emits a structured audit record (JSON line) to an append-only store; each record includes event id, sequence number, HSM attestation token, and sha256(prev_record|event_payload). We provide a bundle for auditors (signed manifest + checkpoints).

Mutual action plan (MAP) — proposed: 
1) 2026-09-09: kickoff with AtlasMed security + infra (30m)
2) 2026-09-13: design review (sequence + network egress rules) — produce finalized diagrams
3) 2026-09-20: staging runbook & failover dry-run (customer participates)
4) 2026-09-27: evidence handoff & compliance artefact delivery

Attachments included: custody-assurance-matrix.xlsx, ephemeral-kek-sequence-diagram.png, and a short attestation snippets doc.

Notes / constraints:
- Fallback KEK lifetime is configurable but we recommend max 7 days while escrowed; automatic re-escrow if not consumed.
- Audit retention: default 365 days with export to customer SIEM available; longer archival via S3 export can be configured.

I've attached the artifacts. Laura, Karthik — tagging you for scheduling and any infra constraints.

Best,

Quick technical clarifications before kickoff: 

- Network: for private VPC, HSM cluster endpoints are reachable via dedicated transit subnet; we require outbound TCP 443 to our attestation service (attest.redwood-inference.net) and TCP 10250-10256 between operator bastion and HSM proxy for heartbeat. No inbound SSH to HSM hosts.

- HSM and KMS policies: fallback KEK is created with origin=HSM, key_usage=unwrapOnly, and policy that denies decrypt unless two attestation tokens present. Rotation is performed by HSM-managed key versioning. We will provide a policy JSON during design review.

- Dry-run behavior: during the staged failover we will use a test-only escrow KEK. The operator action will create an audit record and set a checkpoint; the customer delegate must approve within the 30-minute window. If approval not received the KEK is automatically re-escrowed.

- Audit evidence format: we emit newline-delimited JSON with fields {event_id, ts, actor, event_type, attestation_token, prev_hash, sig}. We support sending logs to your SIEM over TLS and offering a signed manifest file (detached signature) for audit periods.

Attaching a short playbook snippet: ephemeral-keyplaybook.md — contains the CLI sequence for simulated escrow/unseal and the expected audit record.

See you on the kickoff.

Karthik Iyer
Lead Infrastructure Architect, Private Deployments
